blocks.prompt: 3. If both \(x\) and \(y\) are positive distinct real numbers, show that the geometric mean between \(x\) and \(y\) is less than their arithmetic mean.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof (saboot) wala sawal hai: dikhana hai ke \(G < A\). "Distinct" ka matlab hai dono numbers mukhtalif hain, yani \(x \neq y\).
Kisi number ko doosre se chhota saabit karne ka aasan tareeqa yeh hai ke un ka farq (difference) \(A - G\) positive dikha diya jaye.
Plan: \(A - G\) ko ek fraction banayenge aur upar perfect square pehchanenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(x > 0\), \(y > 0\), \(x \neq y\).
Saabit karna hai: \(G < A\).
Tareeqa: A.M. \(A = \frac{x+y}{2}\) (jama kar ke aadha) aur positive G.M. \(G = \sqrt{xy}\). Hum dikhayenge ke \(A - G > 0\). Farq wala tareeqa is liye chuna kyunke kisi cheez ka positive hona dikhana aasan hai, khaas taur par jab woh kisi square ki shakal mein aa jaye.

\(A - G\) ko ek fraction banayein
\[A - G = \dfrac{x + y}{2} - \sqrt{xy}\]
\[= \dfrac{x + y - 2\sqrt{xy}}{2}\]
Kyun: Common denominator 2 liya. \(\sqrt{xy}\) ko \(\frac{2\sqrt{xy}}{2}\) likha taake dono terms ek hi fraction mein aa jayein.

Upar perfect square pehchanein
\[x + y - 2\sqrt{xy}\]
\[= (\sqrt{x})^{2} + (\sqrt{y})^{2} - 2\sqrt{x}\sqrt{y}\]
\[= (\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y})^{2}\]
Kyun: Positive numbers ke liye \(x = (\sqrt{x})^{2}\) aur \(y = (\sqrt{y})^{2}\), aur \(\sqrt{xy} = \sqrt{x}\sqrt{y}\). Ab yeh bilkul formula \((p - q)^{2} = p^{2} - 2pq + q^{2}\) ki shakal hai, jahan \(p = \sqrt{x}\), \(q = \sqrt{y}\). Yahi is proof ka asal "trick" hai.

Sign ka faisla karein
\[A - G = \dfrac{(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y})^{2}}{2}\]
\[> 0\]
Kyun: \(x \neq y\) hai, is liye \(\sqrt{x} \neq \sqrt{y}\), yani \(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y}\) zero nahi. Kisi bhi non-zero real number ka square hamesha positive hota hai, aur positive ko 2 se divide karein to positive hi rehta hai.
Dhyan dein: Yahan "distinct" wali shart bohat zaroori hai; agar \(x = y\) hota to square zero hota aur sirf \(A = G\) milta.

Natija nikalein
\[A - G > 0\]
\[\Rightarrow G < A\]
Kyun: Jab \(A\) mein se \(G\) nikalne par positive bache, to \(A\) bara hai aur \(G\) chhota.

Tasdeeq: numbers se check karein
\[x = 1,\ y = 9:\ A = 5,\ G = 3\]
Kyun: \(3 < 5\), bilkul jaisa saabit kiya. Agar \(x = y\) ho to square zero aur \(A = G\); yahi kitab ke 6.6.1 wala natija hai: \(A > G\) jab \(a \neq b\), aur \(A = G\) jab \(a = b\).
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(G < A\), kyunke \(A - G = \frac{(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y})^{2}}{2} > 0\).
